4.read_extent: Complete Definition of Lambda(theta) as an improper log-sine integral.

empty: checked
The interval has zero length when theta=0, yielding Lambda(0)=0 by the integral convention; no empty manifold is an input.
zero: checked
At theta=0 the defining integral is zero, and near any k*pi its integrand is log|u-k*pi|+O(1), an integrable singularity.

Theta=1 is an ordinary real argument, not a cardinality-one case or a separate normalization in the definition.
degenerate: checked
The only singular parameters in the integral are zeros of sin(u); local logarithmic growth is integrable, so the improper interpretation is finite.
endpoints: checked
At a sine zero occurring as the upper or lower endpoint, the one-sided integral of log|u-k*pi| converges; negative theta uses oriented integration.
nonempty-choice: not_applicable
For each fixed real theta the integral specifies a unique number; no selection from nonempty sets is involved.
iff-forward: not_applicable

iff-reverse: not_applicable
The log-sine integral does not claim to characterize theta from Lambda(theta), so no reverse implication is asserted.
